quiz.q: Why does Hungary's 20 Oct refusal on Ukraine's clusters 4 and 5 matter, even though clusters 2 and 3 had just opened?
options: It formally ends Ukraine's candidate status
It moves Ukraine's talks from the Council to the European Parliament
It shows that unanimity lets a single member slow accession at every step, even after a deal
It means Moldova must now negotiate separately from Ukraine
quiz.explain: EU accession needs unanimous approval at each stage. [[p:Péter Magyar]]'s government lifted one veto after a minority-rights deal, then held back the next step, so every cluster can become a new bargaining point.

quiz.q: Why are European capitals uneasy about Trump's Russian diesel deal?
options: It forces EU states to buy Russian diesel
It eases US sanctions pressure on Moscow while the EU is still tightening its own
It cancels the EU's latest sanctions listings
It moves Ukraine peace talks to Moscow
quiz.explain: The deal and the 16 Oct waiver of Graham Act sanctions open a gap between US and EU policy, which weakens the shared pressure on Russia. [[p:Kaja Kallas]] said the EU would keep sanctioning Russia.

quiz.q: What links the Iran war to France's protests and bond yields?
options: Iran directly funds French protest groups
The ECB raised rates to punish France
France is a party to the Iran war
The Hormuz closure pushed up oil and gas prices, feeding cost-of-living anger and straining budgets
quiz.explain: With Hormuz closed, Brent passed $117 and TTF gas €90. Higher energy costs fuel protests, and they also squeeze governments such as France's that are already struggling to pass budgets, which pushes up borrowing costs.

quiz.q: Why is the Oleshky ceasefire seen as significant despite being local?
options: Both general staffs agreed to the same start time, a rare joint step ahead of wider talks
It ends fighting along the whole Kherson front
It returns Oleshky to Ukrainian control
It was negotiated by the UN Security Council
quiz.explain: Russia's and Ukraine's general staffs both committed to 27 Oct. It is a small, testable agreement before trilateral talks expected in Abu Dhabi in November. Its scope and end date remain unclear.

quiz.q: Why does the UN Secretary-General race look stuck, even though Rebeca Grynspan leads the straw polls?
options: The General Assembly must approve each straw poll
Candidates must come from the Security Council's members
Every candidate has drawn a 'discourage' vote from at least one veto-holding member
The current Secretary-General can veto successors
quiz.explain: The Council recommends a candidate, and any of the five permanent members can block one. With objections against all candidates, new entrants such as the UAE's Lana Nusseibeh are still joining the race.
